root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: digging or removing material downward, and the beginning or original state to which something returns.
root_idea.development: From excavation come terms for pits, excavated material, digging tools, and the hoof understood as striking or digging the ground. A secondary development concerns erosion, deterioration, and return to an initial state; the latter is Quranically attested in حَافِرَة.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized noun حَافِرَةٌ, the Quranic form in 79:10.
Displayed as the normalized noun حُفْرَةٌ, the Quranic form in 3:103.

senses.definition: The first or original state, creation, or condition to which one is returned; in the Quranic context, restoration after death.
senses.usage_conditions: In فِي الْحَافِرَةِ, the expression is understood as return to the initial condition, with the Quranic discussion specifying interpretations such as renewed life, return to the former worldly condition, or restoration to the first creation.

senses.definition: The burial ground or graves—the place in which the dead are laid.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative Quranic interpretation of فِي الْحَافِرَةِ in 79:10, treating the term as the place of burial rather than the state of return itself.

senses.definition: A pit, hollow, or cavity dug in the ground.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَى شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ, the noun denotes a dug hollow or pit; the surrounding phrase describes being on its brink.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig, excavate, hollow out, or clear the ground, a well, a river, or a similar channel; also, to dig for an animal in order to bring it out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used transitively with the ground and excavated objects, and may also be used of burrowing or digging into a hole.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a torrent, to furrow or channel a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of digging, applied to the action of flowing water on a valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction likening the action to a man digging a river.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fathom or determine the full extent of something, especially in the expression describing rain whose extent cannot be known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiomatic use applied to exceptionally deep or extensive rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To investigate an affair and become acquainted with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of penetrating or digging into a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To emaciate or render lean.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is extended to effects attributed to pregnancy, a copious flow of milk, or prolonged suckling; these are attestations of the result, not restrictions on the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a child, to shed the milk teeth, or for the milk teeth to loosen before falling out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized dental use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of teeth or the mouth, to become eroded, cankered, or otherwise unsound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition may involve erosion or scaling of the roots, tartar-like incrustation, or cankering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become in a bad, corrupt, or unsound condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader figurative or intransitive extension of deterioration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a jerboa, to go deep into its hole, beyond the reach of being dug out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III use describing deep burrowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assist someone in digging a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes the person assisted and the object dug.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a colt, to shed or loosen its milk teeth before their replacement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage refers especially to the successive pairs of incisors and neighboring teeth as they become loose and fall out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a torrent, to make hollows in the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V development describing the formation of depressions by flowing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or desire another person to dig a well, pit, channel, or similar excavation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X verb expresses seeking or requesting the digging action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a river, rivulet, or canal, to become due for digging or clearing out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form X use applied to a channel requiring excavation or maintenance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Emaciation or leanness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use corresponding to the verbal sense of rendering lean.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Erosion, scaling, decay, or cankering of the roots or surfaces of the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote tartar-like accumulation, erosion of the roots, yellowness, or another unsound dental condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well widened beyond its ordinary measure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal description of an unusually expanded well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The earth removed from an excavation, or an excavated place such as a moat or well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote either the material taken out or the place that has been dug.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow or cavity in the ground, including a natural hollow or a burrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Unlike the Quranic pit sense, this broader Classical use does not require that the cavity have been made by human digging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dug, excavated, hollowed out, or cleared; especially, a newly dug well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived description of something made by excavation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use distinct from the general sense of something excavated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Material dug out of a mine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use for excavated mineral or earth material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grave-digger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent noun for one who digs graves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A digger or one who digs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun derived from the basic digging sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The solid hoof of a horse, mule, or ass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is understood by comparison with the hoof's striking or digging the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels and horses, by reference to their hoofs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A synecdochic collective use in which the hoof stands for the animal possessing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A human foot characterized as ugly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied specifically when the foot's unattractive appearance is intended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom عِنْدَ الْحَافِرَةِ or عِنْدَ الْحَافِرِ, immediately, at the outset, or upon the first exchange; traditionally, with ready payment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer to payment before leaving the place of sale, the first words spoken, the first meeting, or the first fall of a horse's hoof on dug ground at a race; it consequently extends to priority generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The route by which one came, in the expression for returning by one's former path.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In رَجَعَ عَلَى حَافِرَتِهِ, the term denotes retracing the way of arrival or departure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A former condition of youth, in the expression for becoming old and decrepit or returning to second childishness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional figurative use related to returning to an earlier state, but it is distinct from the Quranic resurrection interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spade or other implement for digging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related forms مِحْفَرَةٌ and مِحْفَارٌ denote the same type of digging tool.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Furrowed, rutted, or hollowed by the passage of people or animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to roads or paths much marked by repeated foot traffic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a pimple or small pustule in the gum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a child affected by this gum condition.
